title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbooks
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood Inference's SRE standards for SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning guidance, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling expectations, and canonical runbooks. It is intended for on-call SREs, owners of serving/runtime services, and product/engineering stakeholders responsible for reliability and capacity commitments.

## Goals
- Establish consistent, measurable SLOs that map to user-visible outcomes.
- Define standardized error budget processes and automation for rollouts and mitigations.
- Provide a repeatable capacity planning process tied to traffic forecasts and cost targets.
- Document incident review standards and postmortem expectations to drive continuous improvement.
- Centralize operational tooling and runbook practices to reduce time-to-recovery (TTD/MTTR).

## Scope
Applies to all customer-facing inference services (hosted API, Redwood Dedicated control plane, and core serving runtime). Internal infra services (CI/CD, internal analytics) should align to these patterns where applicable but may have modified SLO targets.

## Definitions
- SLO (Service Level Objective): measurable target for an SLI over a defined rolling window.
- SLI (Service Level Indicator): the metric collected to evaluate SLO compliance (e.g., successful responses, p95 latency).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO; the tolerated fraction of errors in the measurement window.
- Measurement window: the rolling time window used to evaluate SLOs (default 30d unless noted).

## SLO and Error Budget Standards
1) Required SLOs (applies to inference endpoints):
   - Availability (success rate): 99.95% over 30d (example target for hosted API production tier).
   - Latency: p95 latency <= 200ms for short text-generation endpoints (<=512 tokens) across the last 30d.
   - Model correctness / quality SLOs: pass rate on evaluation prompt-set >= 98% per release (tracked per model).

2) Measurement and aggregation
   - SLIs must be defined at the route/model level and aggregated to service-level dashboards.
   - Primary measurement window: 30d rolling. Secondary window: 7d rolling for rapid detection.
   - All SLI collection uses unified tracing and metrics pipeline (Prometheus/OpenTelemetry -> Cortex -> Grafana).

3) Error budget policy
   - Thresholds:
     * Green: remaining error budget > 50% — normal operations.
     * Yellow: 10% < remaining <= 50% — restrict risky releases; require canary and tenured automation.
     * Red: remaining <= 10% — freeze feature rollouts that increase risk; trigger remediation and mitigation plan.
   - Automatic actions: integrate error-budget gating into the CI/CD release pipeline (canary progression blocked when in Red).
   - Communication: on-change notifications to product and engineering slack channels and the SRE on-call.

4) Ownership and review cadence
   - Each service must have an SLO owner (primary/secondary) listed in the service README.
   - SLOs and error-budget burn rates reviewed weekly in SRE sync and quarterly in reliability review with product.

## Capacity Planning Guidance
Purpose: ensure predictable capacity for traffic spikes, model rollouts, and seasonal events while balancing cost.

1) Inputs and data sources
   - Ingress traffic forecasts (product roadmaps, marketing events).
   - Historical p95/p99 token/req distributions from telemetry.
   - Model CPU/GPU utilization profiles (from performance matrix and past runs).
   - Lead time for provisioning (cloud GPUs, Dedicated pools).

2) Process (quarterly baseline + sprint-level adjustments)
   - Quarterly (90-day) planning:
     1. Collect forecasts and historical telemetry.
     2. Run capacity model: multiply peak QPS forecast by safety margin (default 1.5x) and translate into GPU/replica counts using model profiles.
     3. Produce capacity request (type, region, quantity) and submit to infra procurement 30d before need.
   - Sprint-level (2-week) checks: verify scheduled rollouts and bursts; adjust autoscaler targets.

3) Capacity rules and thresholds (table represented as bullet entries):
   - Baseline headroom: maintain 25% spare capacity for production-hosted endpoints outside of scheduled maintenance.
   - Emergency headroom: ensure ability to absorb a 2x short-term (10-min) burst for critical routes via autoscaling and burst pools.
   - Pre-rollout requirement: allocate canary capacity (>= 10% of target traffic) in the target region for model swaps.

4) Autoscaling and throttling
   - Autoscaling should be workload-aware (token-length, model latency). Use continuous batching knobs when supported.
   - Global throttles for non-critical customers to protect SLOs under extreme load; quota buckets must be respected by API layer.

## Reliability Initiatives and KPIs
- Quarterly reliability themes should be costed and prioritized in the SRE roadmap. Examples: improved KV cache hit rate, lower tail latency for 8k models, faster model swap times.
- OKRs/KPIs to track: average MTTR, p95 latency, error budget burn rate, successful canary ratio, cache hit rate.
- Example initiative: "Reduce p99 latency for short prompt generation by 30%" — includes kernel tuning, batching improvements, and canary testing plan.

## Incident Review Standards (Postmortems)
1) Timeline and ownership
   - Initial incident summary posted within 2 business hours to the incident channel.
   - Full postmortem published within 72 hours for Sev 2/1 incidents.
   - Owner: on-call SRE owns the postmortem; service owner co-authors remediation.

2) Required postmortem sections (use this template):
   - Title and incident summary (1–2 sentences).
   - Impact: affected services, customers, duration, user-visible impact.
   - Timeline: precise events with timestamps.
   - Root cause analysis: technical and systemic causes.
   - Action items: prioritized, with owners and due dates (RACI).
   - Error budget impact and whether burn blocked rollouts.
   - Detect, Mitigate, Prevent: what detected it, how it was mitigated, long-term prevention.

3) Blamelessness and follow-up
   - Postmortems are blameless and focused on system/process changes.
   - All action items tracked in the reliability board and reviewed weekly until complete.

## Operational Tooling Requirements
1) Metrics and dashboards
   - Every service must publish a health dashboard with: key SLIs (availability, latency), resource utilization (GPU/CPU/mem), queue/backlog, request size distribution, and error budget status.
   - Dashboards to include drill-down links to traces and logs for common failure modes (OOM, timeouts, kernel errors).

2) Alerts and paging
   - Alert thresholds mapped to paged vs non-paged:
     * Paged (pager): service-level availability breach, rapid error budget burn (>5% budget/hour), critical autoscaling failures.
     * Non-paged: steady-state threshold breaches (p95 increased), single non-critical partition errors.
   - Alert content should include: short summary, impact, recent relevant Grafana links, runbook link, suggested next steps.

3) Runbook registry and versioning
   - All runbooks stored in the confluence runbook directory and linked from service READMEs.
   - Runbooks must include last-tested date and test owner. Review cadence: every 6 months.

4) Release gating and CI/CD integration
   - CI/CD pipelines must check error-budget status prior to promoting canaries to prod.
   - Automated rollback policies for canaries that breach p95/p99 latency or increase error rate beyond configured thresholds.

## Canonical Runbook Templates
Each runbook must follow this header and sections (plain text):
- Runbook name (Service - incident type)
- Owner, severity, last-tested
- Pager contact and escalation path
- Preconditions / detection signals
- Immediate mitigation steps (ordered)
- Diagnosis steps and useful queries/commands
- Rollback and recovery steps
- Post-incident follow-up and links

Example runbook: Serving runtime - High tail-latency (p99 > 2s)
- Owner: serving-runtime team (primary: on-call-runtime@redwood.com)
- Pager: P1 if > 5% requests exceed p99 threshold for 5m
- Detection: Grafana alert `serving.p99_latency > 2000ms` (5m window)
- Immediate mitigation:
  1. Check overall capacity: `kubectl get hpa -n serving` and GPU utilization dashboards.
  2. If autoscaler stuck, trigger manual scale: increase replica count by +30% and monitor.
  3. For model-level issues: route traffic to a lower-cost model variant (traffic-splitting) using the routing service.
- Diagnosis steps:
  - Correlate traces for high-latency requests (trace IDs).
  - Check kernel and GPU error logs for OOM or compute stalls.
  - Run `promql` queries: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(serving_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))`
- Recovery and rollback:
  - If a recent rollout coincides with burn, rollback the release via the deployment pipeline.
  - If caused by resource exhaustion, add temporary capacity and schedule follow-up.
- Post-incident steps: update runbook, list action items and owners.

Example runbook: GPU pool saturated (Dedicated)
- Owner: gpu-fleet-and-capacity (primary: gpu-fleet@redwood.com)
- Pager: P1 if GPU allocation throttles > 10% for 30m
- Immediate mitigation:
  1. Check scheduled maintenance and pending reservations in the pool UI.
  2. Move non-critical workloads to burst pool or reduce batch sizes.
  3. If capacity cannot be reclaimed, enact cross-region failover for committed customers.

## Testing and Runbook Drills
- Runbook drills (game-days) scheduled quarterly; each on-call rotates ownership for at least one drill per quarter.
- Drill results and action items logged in the reliability board; runbook modifications applied within 2 sprints.

## Reporting and Review
- Weekly SRE report includes: top incident summaries, error budget consumption by service, capacity requests, and open postmortem actions.
- Quarterly reliability review: SLO posture, major incidents, completed initiatives, and roadmap for next quarter.

- Primary owner: Maya Patel (SRE lead) — contact maya.patel@redwood.ai

If you are the owner of a service and do not have SLOs defined in this format, open a ticket in the reliability board and schedule a SLO-writing session with SRE.
